rationale: The assistant correctly refused to name a part blind, sent the customer to the sensible first checks (filter, vent hose, heat programme), and kept a well-calibrated differential of 'tripped thermal cut-out' versus 'failed heating element'. However, in the final turn it ignored the customer's clear statements that they have no multimeter and cannot easily reach the rear label, offering only 'pull the machine forward safely (switched off first)' and never recommending an engineer or explaining that the cut-out/element must be tested before any part is bought. No fabrication, no unsafe instruction and no unjustified part, but the conversation stalled with the key question ('Can you work it out from DV7110?') unanswered and no route forward for a customer who cannot test.
